items.context: You are a member of your local library. You received this email from the library.
items.situation: From 1 March, the library will no longer open on Sundays. The money saved will pay for a new self-service system. There will also be fewer staff on duty on weekday evenings.

informal.prompt: Write an email to a friend who is also a member of the library. Tell your friend about the change and say how you feel about it. Write about 40–50 words.

b2.text:
Hi Marta,

Have you read the library's email? They're closing on Sundays from March! I'm really fed up, because Sunday is the only day I can study there in peace. Shall we ask them to open one Sunday a month? Let me know.

Speak soon,
Lola

note.en: 'Fed up' is an informal phrasal expression meaning 'annoyed'.
note.es: 'Fed up' es informal y significa 'harta'.

annotations.quote: because Sunday is the only day

note.en: 'Because' gives the reason for your reaction.
note.es: 'Because' explica el motivo de tu reacción.

note.en: 'Shall we' is a friendly way to make a suggestion.
note.es: 'Shall we' es una forma amistosa de proponer algo.

note.en: A warm, informal sign-off.
note.es: Una despedida cálida e informal.

c.text:
Hi Marta,

Seen the library's email? Apparently they're scrapping Sundays from March, which is a real blow. It's the only day I can get any proper studying done there. I'd put up with fewer staff if it meant keeping the doors open. Fancy signing a petition?

Cheers,

formal.prompt: Write an email to the Library Manager. Give your opinion of the change and make some suggestions. Write 120–150 words.

b2.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to express my concern about the decision to close the library on Sundays from 1 March.

I have been a member for five years and I visit almost every Sunday, because I work from Monday to Saturday. For people like me, it is the only day when I can borrow books and use the study room. I also think that students who need a quiet place before their exams will be badly affected.

I understand that the library needs a self-service system, but I believe there are other ways to save money. For example, you could open only in the afternoon on Sundays, or you could reduce the weekday evening hours instead. I would also be happy to pay a small annual fee.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Lola Vega

note.en: A clear formal opening that states the purpose in the first line.
note.es: Apertura formal que declara el propósito en la primera línea.

annotations.quote: because I work from Monday to Saturday

note.en: 'Because' introduces a clear reason.
note.es: 'Because' introduce una razón clara.

annotations.quote: I understand that the library needs

note.en: Acknowledging the other side makes a complaint sound polite.
note.es: Reconocer el otro punto de vista hace la queja más cortés.

note.en: 'For example' introduces a concrete suggestion.
note.es: 'For example' introduce una sugerencia concreta.

note.en: The standard formal closing sentence.

c.text:
Dear Ms Carter,

I am writing in connection with the announcement that the library will cease to open on Sundays from 1 March.

I fully appreciate the need to modernise, and a self-service system would doubtless be welcome. Nevertheless, I am concerned that this decision will fall hardest on those who work during the week; Sunday is, for many of us, the only day on which the library is realistically accessible. Nor, I suspect, will students preparing for examinations be well served by the change.

It is the loss of the study room that troubles me most. Might I therefore suggest opening on Sunday afternoons only, with staffing reduced on weekday mornings instead? Should further savings prove necessary, a modest annual fee would be preferable to a complete closure.

I would be grateful if you would consider these points.

Yours sincerely,
Lola Vega

note.en: A formal opening phrase that states the purpose at once.
note.es: Apertura formal que indica el propósito de inmediato.

annotations.quote: the only day on which the library is realistically accessible

note.en: Preposition + 'which' is a formal relative clause.
note.es: Preposición + 'which': oración de relativo formal.

note.en: Inversion after 'nor', with a hedge in the middle.
note.es: Inversión tras 'nor', con una cautela intercalada.

annotations.quote: It is the loss of the study room that troubles me most.

note.en: A cleft sentence that puts the focus on the real problem.
note.es: Oración hendida que pone el foco en el problema real.

note.en: Inverted conditional with 'should' instead of 'if'.
note.es: Condicional invertido con 'should' en lugar de 'if'.

annotations.quote: I would be grateful if you would

note.en: A polite, indirect request used in formal letters.
note.es: Petición indirecta y cortés propia de cartas formales.

items.context: You are a member of a local cycling club. You received this email from the club.
items.situation: From April, the club's Saturday morning rides will move to Wednesday evenings, because fewer volunteers are available at weekends. Every ride will also be limited to 30 kilometres so that everyone is home before dark.

informal.prompt: Write an email to a friend who is also a member of the club. Tell your friend about the change and say how you feel about it. Write about 40–50 words.

b2.text:
Hi Dan,

Seen the club's email? The Saturday rides are moving to Wednesday evenings from April! I can't believe it, because I never finish work before seven. I'm gutted. Shall we organise our own ride on Saturdays? Give me a ring to sort it out.

Speak soon,
Paul

c.text:
Hi Dan,

Have you seen the club's email? The Saturday rides are being shifted to Wednesday evenings from April, and frankly I'm gutted. There's no way I'll get away from the office. Still, it needn't be the end of it: why not set up our own weekend group?

Cheers,
Paul

formal.prompt: Write an email to the Club Secretary. Give your opinion of the change and make some suggestions. Write 120–150 words.

b2.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the decision to move the Saturday morning rides to Wednesday evenings from April.

I have belonged to the club for four years and the Saturday ride is the highlight of my week. On Wednesdays I do not finish work until seven, so I would not be able to take part at all. In addition, I think a limit of thirty kilometres is too short for experienced cyclists, who need longer routes to prepare for events.

I understand that it is difficult to find volunteers at weekends. However, I would like to suggest that the club keeps one Saturday ride a month, led by members who are willing to help. Another possibility is to offer a short Wednesday ride and a longer one on Sundays.

I hope you will think about these ideas.

Yours faithfully,
Paul Hill

c.text:
Dear Mr Okafor,

I am writing in response to your announcement that the Saturday rides will be replaced by Wednesday evening outings from April.

While I fully appreciate the difficulty of recruiting volunteers at weekends, I cannot help feeling that the proposal fails to take account of members who work until the early evening. Not only would I be unable to attend on Wednesdays, but the thirty-kilometre limit would also leave experienced riders without adequate preparation for sportives.

It is the loss of the weekend ride that concerns me most. I would therefore urge the committee to retain a monthly Saturday outing, with ride leaders drawn from the membership on a rota basis. Alternatively, a short midweek route could run alongside a longer Sunday one, which would address both safety and demand.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss this further.

Yours sincerely,
Paul Hill

items.context: You are a regular user of a city bike-hire scheme. You received this email from the scheme.
items.situation: From 1 June, the daily price will rise from one pound to three pounds, and the first thirty minutes will no longer be free. Eight docking stations in the suburbs will also close, because too few people use them.

informal.prompt: Write an email to a friend who also uses the scheme. Tell your friend about the changes and say how you feel about them. Write about 40–50 words.

b2.text:
Hi Sara,

Have you seen CityBikes' email? From June it'll cost three pounds a day, and they're closing eight stations in the suburbs. I'm really annoyed, because I ride to work every day. Let's write to them together and make them think again!

See you soon,
Tom

b2.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing about the changes to the bike-hire scheme that you announced in your recent email.

I have used the scheme every working day for two years, and I live in a suburb where a docking station will close. If the daily price rises to three pounds, I will pay much more than I do now, and I will have to walk a long way to the nearest station. I think many people will stop using the bikes, which would be bad for the city and the environment.

I understand that the scheme needs more money. However, I would suggest keeping the first thirty minutes free, or offering a cheaper monthly pass for regular users. I would also ask you to keep open the stations that serve the most commuters.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Tom Reed

c.text:
Dear Ms Hollis,

I am writing regarding the revised pricing structure and the planned closure of eight suburban docking stations, as outlined in your recent email.

As a daily user, I am seriously concerned that these measures will prove counterproductive. Tripling the daily charge is likely to deter precisely those commuters on whom the scheme depends, while the closure of suburban stations will leave residents such as myself without a practical alternative to the car.

Though I appreciate the pressure on your finances, I would suggest retaining the free half-hour, which encourages short, frequent journeys. A discounted monthly pass for regular riders would also be a fair compromise. Moreover, any closures should be based on usage at peak commuting times, not on overall figures.

I would be most grateful if you would reconsider the proposals before they come into force.

Yours sincerely,
Tom Reed
